messages:
alex: kicking off deploy to canary group for service router (v4.2.1) in 5m. change window 11:00-11:30 PT. refer runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-safety-latch

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started — 5% on pool-3 (instance group a)

priya: what's our escape-latch thresholds? need exact metrics so oncall can abort quickly :eyes:

alex: agreed. thresholds per runbook: error-rate >= 1.5% sustained over 2m OR p95 latency > 800ms OR memory OOMs on >2 pods. manual abort command: `rd-deploy abort --env prod --tag v4.2.1`
Pin back to stable: `rd-deploy pin --service router --version v4.2.0`
Also rollback-safe steps in runbook: disable traffic, pin, scale down new pool, promote old pool.

sam: add note: if canary fails, also disable kv-cache feature-flag `kv-cache-v2` and restart router pods (graceful drain)

deploy-bot: Canary at 20% — no errors so far. metrics snapshot: err 0.12% p95 210ms

kim: I'm on the bridge and watching metrics. have runbook open. if thresholds hit before 11:10 i'll abort; otherwise leave decision to oncall after 11:10

alex: operational decision: if any threshold trips, abort and follow runbook section "escape-latch-quick-path". If borderline (p95 spike but < 2m sustained), hold at current canary and escalate to infra. logging decision path in /ops/deploys/2026-03-20-v4.2.1

oncall-rota: ack — standby on paging

deploy-bot: Canary progressed to 100% at 1978001298 — rollout metrics: err 0.08% p95 195ms, no OOMs. Rolling stable tag update now.

priya: leaving post-deploy smoke checklist here: 1) /health endpoints green, 2) batch jobs backfilled, 3) billing ingest sanity, 4) caches warmed, 5) alerting thresholds validated

alex: thanks all. if any post-deploy regressions, follow runbook rollback section and open incident channel. closing thread and will paste summary to #eng-releases.
